text.p: Following is a fact file on England defender Stuart Pearce who joined Newcastle from Nottingham Forest on Friday.
1983: After training as an electrician and playing for non-League Wealdstone, signed by Bobby Gould in October for Coventry for 25,000 pounds ($37,500). Makes 54 appearances, scoring four goals.
1985: In June signs for Nottingham Forest in 200,000 pounds ($300,000) deal, making his debut at Luton on August 17. Goes on to make 503 appearances so far for Forest, scoring 85 goals.
1986: Makes a solitary appearance for England Under-21s -- as an over-age player -- against Yugoslavia in November.
1987: Takes over as Forest captain and in May makes full England debut in 1-1 draw with Brazil at Wembley.
1990: Wins second League Cup winners' medal but career hits low point in Turin in July with his penalty miss in England's shoot-out defeat by Germany in World Cup semifinal.
1991: Scores in FA Cup final at Wembley but Forest lose to Tottenham.
1992: Takes over as England captain from Gary Lineker.

1996: Features in England's Euro96 campaign, including scoring penalty in shoot-out victory over Spain in quarterfinals. Retires from international football after collecting 70th cap in European Championship semifinal defeat by Germany at Wembley.

New England coach Glenn Hoddle talks him out of international retirement for World Cup qualifying match in Moldova on September 1, and he also plays against Poland in October to win his 72nd cap. Appointed caretaker-manager of Forest on December 20 until mid-January following resignation of Frank Clark.
1997: Appointed caretaker manager until end of the season in January, leading Forest to six wins out of his first nine games in charge. Forest relegated.
Joins Newcastle on three-year free transfer deal.
